contract.purpose: Reverse-lookup registry of instruments. The point is not 'what does this script measure' -- the filename usually implies that, and usually implies too much. The point is `conditioned_on` and `cannot_answer`: what the instrument silently holds fixed, and which questions it is therefore structurally unable to answer no matter how many times it is run.
contract.rule: cannot_answer is mandatory and must name questions somebody could plausibly believe this instrument settles. An empty cannot_answer means the entry has not been thought through. Conditioning that is invisible in the output is the failure mode this registry exists to prevent: measure_anchor_recall applies the item cap before enumerating, so it reads as an oracle over placements when it is an oracle over placements *of the ten items the cap admitted*.

scripts/build_branch_labels.py.note: The first instrument on this repository that produces a long-horizon paired label. Every earlier board-value label was short-horizon and is known unusable: placed-to-go is confounded by step and volume, immediate settle survival is unrelated to option counts, and 95.2% of Q-band sibling pairs tie on any short-horizon outcome.
